newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian presidential elections - final results.
newsitem.headline: Romanian presidential elections - final results.

text.p: Centrist academic Emil Constantinescu won Romania's presidential election with more than 54 percent of the votes, according to final results released on Tuesday.
The Central Electoral Bureau said Constantinescu, who turned 57 on Tuesday, received 7.06 million votes in the run-off, or 54.41 percent.
Ex-communist incumbent Ion Iliescu won 5.91 million votes, or 45.59 percent in Sunday's poll.
Turnout was 75.90 percent of Romania's 17.3 million voters. Fewer than one percent of votes cast were declared invalid, despite wide fears of vote rigging and technical problems.

Constantinescu's win completed the rout of leftists in Romania's 1996 election year. Centrists ousted Iliescu's party from major city halls in the local polls last June and from government in the parliamentary elections earlier this month.
